detail: With the new CGP Follow-ups plugin installed, the follow-up issues of your session show in a row of the CGP Effort bar, with their status kept up to date from Jira, GitHub or Linear.

note: Cheaper when it can, priced per turn
detail: Routing to a cheaper model now weighs the whole turn on current API rates and only moves when it saves at least 10 %. /cgp-effort stats shows the estimated saving.
A key pasted in Settings or setup is saved to Claude Code's secure storage again; current Claude Code builds had refused it.
The key goes over standard input only and never shows in a process list.
The key field in Settings and setup shows dots instead of the key.
Until saved, the key stays in the plugin's memory only; afterwards the field shows its last four characters.
In a terminal too narrow for one line, the bar's buttons move to a second line instead of breaking.
The guide and README describe the CGP Crew row.

note: CGP Crew shows in the band
detail: When the cgp-crew plugin runs a crew, it appears in a row above the dashboard instead of a second bar.
The Crew button opens the crew panel, the cross hides the row.
With the Minimal look or without cgp-crew nothing changes.
Picks the reasoning effort for every prompt with Haiku 5.5 on your own Claude login, or Jev with a TypeSafe key.
Shows the effort, the context share and the prompt-cache countdown above the prompt.
Compact and Handoff in one click when a chat gets heavy, with alerts for cold caches, full contexts and usage limits.
A handoff names the next steps and the skills to use, marks what was not checked, links instead of copying, and can be aimed at what comes next.
Auto effort can be switched off for good in Settings without uninstalling.
Optional: keep the prompt cache warm on big chats, and switch animations off.
Runs in the desktop app and the terminal, on macOS, Linux and Windows.
